name: Beaverhead River
blurb: Tailwater below Clark Canyon Dam. Tight, weedy, and technical — drift boats more than tubes.

sections.putIn: Beaverhead River Access (below Clark Canyon Dam)
sections.notes: Launch on the Beaverhead below Clark Canyon Dam, not in the reservoir. Finish at the High Bridge hand launch. Narrow channels and brush can complicate access; inspect the exits during your shuttle.

notices.title: Upper Beaverhead fishing season
notices.text: From Clark Canyon Dam to Pipe Organ Bridge, fishing is open from the third Saturday in May through September 30. Additional tackle and harvest rules apply. This is a fishing-season rule, not a blanket boating closure; check the current FWP regulations before fishing.

putInAccess.sourceName: U.S. Bureau of Reclamation — Clark Canyon recreation brochure

putInAccess.directions: Use the signed Beaverhead River Access below Clark Canyon Dam, reached by the steep gravel road off State Road 324 on the west side of the dam. This is the river launch, separate from the reservoir boat ramps.

takeOutAccess.note: FWP documents hand-launch access. Its former general-site marker is inland. The reviewed OpenStreetMap slipway point is closer to the visible landing; it is an approximate access area, not an agency-confirmed water-edge pin.
takeOutAccess.directions: Reach High Bridge from the recreation road south of Dillon. Look for the signed FWP hand launch beneath the I-15 bridge, beside the river and west of the railway. Check the shoreline approach before shuttling.

notices.title: Take out before the footbridge and diversion dam
notices.text: The Reclamation site plan places the public boat ramp immediately upstream of the footbridge at Barretts Station Park, on the left bank facing downstream. The private vehicle bridge and diversion dam are downstream. Locate and scout the ramp from shore before launching; the approximate marker is not an on-water landing instruction.

takeOutAccess.sourceName: Bureau of Reclamation — Barretts site plan, August 2004; Visit Montana access listing
takeOutAccess.note: The August 2004 Reclamation site drawing labels the boat ramp upstream of the footbridge, consistent with the visible bridges and park approach. Visit Montana still documents a boat take-out. The unchanged OSM north-end footbridge coordinate anchors this approximate area. It is not a ramp survey or proof of current conditions. The rejected tourism coordinate at the diversion dam remains research-only; the campground centroid downstream of the footbridge is also not used.
takeOutAccess.directions: Enter Barretts Station Park from Old Stage Road and follow the public park road to the footbridge. Locate the public boat ramp immediately upstream of the footbridge on the left bank facing downstream during your shuttle. Finish before the footbridge; the private vehicle bridge and diversion dam are farther downstream. This area marker identifies the bridge approach, not the exact landing.

gaugeContext.note: The Barretts station is downstream of these upper trips, upstream of Barretts Diversion Dam. USGS operates it March through October, so a winter reporting gap is expected. Its flow is reference information, not a calibrated speed for these trips.

timing.note: A reviewed flow-to-speed model has not been established for these reaches. Maps and sourced planning distances remain available without a live float-time estimate.

mapAuditNote: All listed sections now have documented approximate access areas. Barretts uses the upstream footbridge approach supported by the Reclamation site plan; exact ramp edges and current conditions still need local checks. Course display and timing are reviewed independently.
